transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, thank you. I'm here because of a problem I have with bridges. It's... well, the moment a bridge crossing becomes unavoidable, my heart just starts pounding. My hands go completely damp on the steering wheel, or the armrest if someone else is driving, and I feel this terrible rush of fear before I’m even on the bridge itself.
Do you get this same rush of fear in other situations besides bridges?

No, not really. I... I don't have that problem anywhere else. I can fly on airplanes, ride in elevators, go up in tall buildings—none of that bothers me in the slightest. It's strictly just the bridges.
Outside of bridge situations, have you ever had a sudden panic attack that seemed to come out of the blue?
No, I haven't. I've never had anything like that happen just out of the blue. It's only when I'm faced with a bridge. Otherwise, I feel completely fine.
